name: Progressions (AP & GP)
intro: **For an AP, find d first and the first term second.** Two given terms always fix d by subtraction, and everything else follows (§1).
The single most useful AP fact: the sum of n terms equals n × (middle term) when n is odd. It turns many "sum of 15 terms" questions into one multiplication (§4).

qs.q: Find the 20th term of the AP 7, 11, 15, …
qs.h: §1 — aₙ = a + (n − 1)d. The trap is using n rather than n − 1.

qs.q: The number of terms in the AP 5, 9, 13, …, 185 is
qs.h: §1 — n = (last − first)/d + 1. Forgetting the +1 is the standard slip.

qs.q: If the 5th term of an AP is 17 and the 9th is 29, find the first term.
qs.h: §1 — the gap between the 5th and 9th terms is 4d, not 5d.

qs.q: In an AP, the sum of the 4th and 12th terms is 40. The sum of the first 15 terms is
qs.h: §4 — terms equidistant from the ends sum to the same value, and the 8th term is the average of the 4th and 12th.

qs.q: The 7th term of an AP is 34 and the 13th is 64. Find the 20th term.
qs.h: §1 — six gaps between the 7th and 13th terms, then seven more to the 20th.

qs.q: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, …
The sum of all two-digit numbers divisible by 7 is
qs.h: §2 — the terms run 14 to 98. Count them first, then use n/2 (first + last).

qs.q: Find the sum of the terms from the 11th to the 20th of the AP 2, 5, 8, …
qs.h: §2 — a term range is S₂₀ − S₁₀. Do not try to build a new AP from scratch.

qs.q: The sum of the first n natural numbers is 210. Then n is
qs.h: §4 — n(n + 1)/2 = 210, so n(n + 1) = 420. Look for consecutive integers near √420.

qs.q: The sum of the first 12 terms of an AP is 390 and the first term is 5. Find the common difference.
qs.h: §2 — substitute into S₁₂ = 6[2a + 11d] and solve the single linear equation.

qs.q: The sum of the first 20 odd natural numbers is
qs.h: §4 — the sum of the first n odd numbers is exactly n².

qs.q: How many terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, … are less than 200?
qs.h: §3 — write the general term, solve the inequality, then take the floor.

qs.q: How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 6?
qs.h: §3 — the range is 102 to 996.

qs.q: How many numbers between 100 and 400 are divisible by both 4 and 6?
qs.h: §3 — divisible by both means divisible by the LCM, 12, not 24.

qs.q: How many terms are common to the APs 2, 5, 8, … and 3, 7, 11, …, taking both only up to 200?
qs.h: §3 — common terms form their own AP whose difference is the LCM of the two differences. Find the first common term by inspection.
qs.s: The first common term is 11, and the common difference is LCM(3, 4) = 12 ⟹ 11, 23, …, 191 ⟹ 16 terms.

qs.q: How many integers strictly between 1 and 500 are divisible by 3 but not by 5?
qs.h: §3 — count the multiples of 3, then subtract the multiples of 15.
qs.s: Multiples of 3: 166 (3 to 498). Multiples of 15: 33 (15 to 495) ⟹ 166 − 33 = 133.

qs.q: Find the 7th term of the GP 3, 6, 12, …
qs.h: §5 — aₙ = ar^(n−1). The exponent is n − 1, not n.

qs.q: The sum of the infinite GP 8, 4, 2, 1, … is
qs.h: §5 — S∞ = a/(1 − r), valid because |r| < 1.

qs.q: Find the sum of the first 6 terms of the GP 2, 6, 18, …
qs.h: §5 — Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) when r > 1.

qs.q: In a GP the 3rd term is 12 and the 6th is 96. The first term is
qs.h: §5 — the ratio of the two given terms is r raised to the gap in positions.

qs.q: The sum of an infinite GP is 15 and the first term is 5. Find the common ratio (as a fraction).
qs.h: §5 — rearrange a/(1 − r) = S.

qs.q: If the arithmetic mean of two numbers is 10 and their geometric mean is 8, the numbers are
qs.h: §5 — sum 20, product 64. They are the roots of a quadratic.

sets.name: Harmonic progressions, means and standard sums

qs.q: Find the harmonic mean of 4 and 12.
qs.h: §6 — HM = 2ab/(a + b). Not the average.

qs.q: If the AM of two numbers is 25 and their HM is 16, their GM is
qs.h: §6 — GM² = AM × HM, the identity worth memorising.

qs.q: Find the sum 1² + 2² + … + 12².
The value of 1³ + 2³ + … + 10³ is
qs.h: §4 — the sum of the first n cubes is the square of the sum of the first n naturals.

qs.q: The 4th term of an HP is 1/12 and the 8th is 1/20. Find the 12th term (as a fraction).
qs.h: §6 — take reciprocals to get an AP, work there, then invert at the very end.
qs.s: Reciprocals: a₄ = 12, a₈ = 20 ⟹ d = 2 ⟹ a₁₂ = 28 ⟹ the HP term is 1/28.

qs.q: Find the sum of all three-digit numbers divisible by 9.
qs.h: Count the terms first, then pair the ends.

qs.q: The 15th term of the AP whose 3rd term is 10 and 7th term is 26 is
qs.h: Four gaps between the 3rd and 7th terms.

qs.q: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is 3n² + 5n. Find its 10th term.
qs.h: aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ — the cleanest route when Sₙ is given directly.

qs.q: The sum of the infinite series 1 + 1/3 + 1/9 + … is
How many two-digit numbers leave a remainder of 3 when divided by 8?
qs.h: The terms run 11, 19, …

qs.q: Three numbers in AP have sum 27 and product 504. The smallest is
qs.h: Write them as a − d, a, a + d; the sum gives a immediately.
qs.s: 3a = 27 ⟹ a = 9 ⟹ 9(81 − d²) = 504 ⟹ d² = 25 ⟹ the numbers are 4, 9, 14 ⟹ smallest = 4.

qs.q: In a GP the 2nd term is 6 and the 5th is 162. Find the 8th term.
qs.h: Three positions apart means r³.

qs.q: The number of terms common to the APs 3, 7, 11, … up to 407 and 2, 9, 16, … up to 709 is
qs.h: Common difference is LCM(4, 7); the upper limit is the smaller of the two ceilings.

qs.q: The sum of the first 15 terms of an AP is 600. Find its 8th term.
qs.h: For an odd number of terms, the sum is n × the middle term.

qs.q: If a, b, c are in GP with a = 2 and c = 32, then the positive value of b is
qs.h: The middle term of a GP is the geometric mean of its neighbours.
qs.s: b² = ac = 64 ⟹ b = 8. (17 is the arithmetic mean — the planted decoy.)

audit: using n instead of n − 1 for the number of gaps (§1, §5)
forgetting the +1 when counting terms in a range (§3)
A4, M9
computing Sₙ the long way where n × (middle term) does it in one step (§4)
B3
rebuilding a new AP for a term range instead of taking the difference of two sums (§2)
C3
using the product of the divisors instead of their LCM
C4, M8
guessing the first common term rather than finding it, or using the wrong upper limit
C5
double-counting the multiples of 15 instead of subtracting them
using the finite-sum formula on an infinite GP, or forgetting the |r| < 1 condition (§5)
D4, M7
taking the ratio of terms as r rather than as r raised to the position gap
E1, E2
using the arithmetic mean where the harmonic or geometric mean is required (§6)
E5
working directly in the HP instead of inverting to an AP first
M3
solving for a and d where aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ is immediate
M6
not centring the three terms on a, which makes the sum condition trivial
using the arithmetic mean for the middle term of a GP
